overview: Ivory Coast, also called Côte d'Ivoire, is a country in West Africa, on the Gulf of Guinea. Its official capital is Yamoussoukro, while Abidjan is its largest city and economic centre. It became independent from France in 1960. French is the official language, and Ivory Coast is the world's largest producer of cocoa.

geography.text: The south of Ivory Coast has a coastline of lagoons and beaches, with tropical rainforest inland. Further north the land becomes savanna on a gently rising plateau. The west is hillier, rising to Mount Nimba on the border with Guinea and Liberia.

history.text: Akan, Kru and other peoples lived in the region, which Europeans named after its ivory trade. France made it a colony in 1893. Côte d'Ivoire became independent in 1960 under Félix Houphouët-Boigny and grew into the world's largest cocoa producer. Two civil wars, in 2002 and 2010–11, divided the country before peace returned.

events.title: French colony
events.text: Côte d'Ivoire becomes a French colony.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Félix Houphouët-Boigny becomes the first president.

events.title: Civil war
events.text: The country is split between north and south.

events.title: Post-election crisis
events.text: Fighting ends with Alassane Ouattara taking office.
